name: Graft
text:
Decision: We should build a single, shared "memory map" that links every key idea to its meaning, its relationships, and the context where it matters. This map will be a living document—updated as we learn—so the brain graph grows naturally as we work.

Why this works: A shared map keeps meaning at the center, not just facts. It forces us to state *why* something matters, which embeds it deeper than isolated notes. The trade-off is speed—we’ll spend time structuring instead of just dumping—but the payoff is recall that lasts.
